title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat, say exactly what's broken and for how long, get the owner to have it fixed, deal with water, power and the building, and keep things friendly with the neighbours.
intro:
Most people in Chennai, Coimbatore or Madurai rent — and renting means talking: to the broker, to the **house owner**, to the plumber, to the watchman and to the family next door. This unit gives you the words for the flat and for everything that goes wrong in it (the tap, the power, the water pump), and two pieces of grammar for getting things sorted: saying clearly **what's wrong and for how long** (ரெண்டு நாளா தண்ணியே வரல 'no water at all for two days'), and the Tamil ways of **getting someone else to do it** — பிளம்பரை வரச் சொல்லுங்க 'get the plumber to come', சரி பண்ணிக் குடுங்க 'fix it for me'.

As in real life, most of the house words are English: flat, advance, maintenance, current, heater, lift. The Tamil verbs that go with them are what make you sound natural.

grammar.title: Saying what's wrong — and for how long
grammar.body:
To report a problem you need three simple tools.

**1. What it's doing: the present tense.** ஒழுகுது *oḻugudu* 'it's leaking', சத்தம் வருது 'there's a noise (lit. a noise comes)'. Fans, pumps and fridges **run** (ஓடு): ஃபேன் ஓடுது 'the fan works'.

**2. What it isn't doing: infinitive + -ல.** The spoken negative ஓடல *ōḍala*, வரல *varala*, வேலை செய்யல *vēlai seyyala* covers both 'isn't' and 'didn't': ஃபேன் ஓடல 'the fan isn't working', தண்ணி வரல 'no water is coming / came'. For **not at all**, add **-ஏ** to the noun or to the verb: தண்ணி**யே** வரல 'not a drop of water', யாரு**மே** வரல 'nobody at all came', வர**வே** இல்ல 'didn't come at all'.

**3. For how long: time word + -ஆ.** ரெண்டு நாள் → ரெண்டு **நாளா** 'for two days', ஒரு வாரமா 'for a week', ரொம்ப நாளா 'for ages'. With the continuous it gives 'have been …-ing': ஒரு வாரமா சொல்லிட்டு இருக்கேன் 'I've been saying it for a week'.

**Polite but firm.** Start soft — கொஞ்சம் பாருங்க 'please have a look' — and get firmer step by step: **-ணும்** 'it has to…' (இன்னைக்கே சரி பண்ணணும் 'it needs fixing today'), then the rhetorical **எத்தனை தடவை சொல்றது?** 'how many times do I have to say it?'. Keep நீங்க and சார் / மேடம் throughout: in Tamil, firmness comes from facts and deadlines, not from dropping the respect — the moment you switch to நீ, it's a quarrel.

examples.en: There's been no water at all for two days.
The heater isn't working, could you take a look?
There's some noise coming from the pump.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting it fixed
grammar.body:
Most of the time you don't fix things yourself — you get the owner, the plumber or the watchman to do it. Spoken Tamil has four everyday ways to say this.

**1. Tell someone to: infinitive + சொல்லு.** பிளம்பரை வரச் சொல்லுங்க 'tell the plumber to come' = 'get the plumber to come'; மோட்டார் போடச் சொன்னேன் 'I told them to switch on the pump'. The person takes **-ஐ** (பிளம்பரை), or **-க்கு** when you mean 'say to' (வாட்ச்மேனுக்குச் சொல்லுங்க 'tell the watchman'). This is the causative you'll hear most.

**2. Make / have someone do: infinitive + வை.** சரி பண்ண வைக்கிறேன் 'I'll get it fixed (I'll make them fix it)', ஆளை வர வைக்கிறேன் 'I'll get someone to come'. It sounds more forceful: you make it happen.

**3. Do it for me: -இ form + குடு.** சரி பண்ணிக் குடுங்க 'fix it for me', மாத்திக் குடுங்க 'replace it for me', திருப்பிக் குடுங்க 'give it back'. Adding குடு turns a bare order into a service you're asking for — exactly what you say to a plumber or a shopkeeper.

**4. Verb pairs.** Many verbs have a 'by itself' partner and a 'make it' partner: மாறு 'change' → **மாத்து** 'change something, replace'; திரும்பு 'come back' → **திருப்பு** 'give back, turn something'; ஓடு 'run' → ஓட்டு 'drive'. Learn them in pairs: the plumber மாத்துவாரு 'will replace (it)', never மாறுவாரு (that would mean he changes as a person!).

Finally **ஆள் வச்சு** 'by putting a person on it' means 'by getting someone in': ஆள் வச்சு பெயிண்ட் அடிக்கணும் 'we need to get someone in to paint'.

examples.en: Get the plumber to come tomorrow morning.

examples.native: வீட்டுக்காரருக்கு ஃபோன் பண்ணி ஹீட்டரை மாத்த வைக்கிறேன்.
examples.roman: vīṭṭukkārarukku fōn paṇṇi hīṭṭarai mātta vaikkirēn.
examples.en: I'll call the owner and get him to replace the heater.
Please replace this switch for me.
We need to get someone in to clean the house.

dialogue.title: The tap that never stops
dialogue.setting: Karthik rents a flat in Velachery, Chennai. On Sunday morning he rings the owner, Mr Raghavan, who lives in Mylapore.

lines.native: ஹலோ, சார், வணக்கம். நான் கார்த்திக், ரெண்டாவது மாடி.

lines.speaker: Karthik

lines.roman: aḍaḍā. sari, namma plambar Muruganai varach solrēn.

lines.speaker: Karthik

lines.speaker: Raghavan

culture:
**Renting** in Tamil Nadu runs on a few unwritten rules. The **advance** is several months' rent (anything from three to ten), paid up front and returned — minus 'painting charges' — when you leave. Many owners ask straight away whether you're a family, what you eat and what you do; **bachelors** (the English word is used) often find it harder to rent, and some buildings are vegetarian-only. Agreements usually run for 11 months.

**Water** is the big topic in Chennai: flats store it in an underground **sump** and a roof tank, someone has to switch on the **motor** to fill it, and in summer people buy tanker lorries of water (தண்ணி லாரி). **Power cuts** (கரண்ட் கட்) are shorter than they used to be, but still a conversation starter.

Neighbours are addressed as family: **அக்கா, அண்ணா** for people around your age, **ஆன்ட்டி, அங்கிள்** for older ones (in English!), and நீங்க always. Complaints are made gently, often as a question, and after some small talk. When a family moves into a new home, they **boil milk** (பால் காய்ச்சுறது) until it overflows, for prosperity, before living there — the housewarming is often just called 'பால் காய்ச்சு'. And when you move, you hire a 'baby elephant' (**குட்டி யானை**), the nickname of the little Tata Ace trucks.

tip.title: Renting talk: -க்கு and English words
tip.body:
- **வாடகைக்கு** 'for rent' (dative): வீடு வாடகைக்கு இருக்கா?
- **மாசத்துக்கு** 'per month': மாசத்துக்கு பதினஞ்சாயிரம் '15,000 a month'.
- **flat, advance, maintenance, broker** are the normal words; the pure Tamil ones (ஒப்பந்தம்) are for documents.
- Owners will ask about you: family? vegetarian? job? Answer politely with நீங்க.

sentences.en: We need a two-room flat.
The rent is fifteen thousand a month.
The deposit is six months' rent.
You have to give the broker one month's rent.
Do we pay maintenance separately?
The agreement is for eleven months.

sentences.native: ஃபிளாட் நல்லா இருக்கு, ஆனா வாடகை ரொம்ப அதிகம்.
sentences.roman: flāṭ nallā irukku, ānā vāḍagai romba adigam.
sentences.en: The flat's nice, but the rent is too high.
Can you bring the rent down a bit?
It's just the two of us, and we're vegetarian.

tip.title: Isn't working: -ல · for (time): -ஆ
tip.body:
- Spoken negative = infinitive + **-ல**: ஓட**ல** 'isn't running', வர**ல** 'isn't coming / didn't come', வேலை செய்ய**ல** 'isn't working'.
- 'Not at all': add **-ஏ**: தண்ணி**யே** வரல, யாரு**மே** வரல.
- 'For two days': time word + **-ஆ**: ரெண்டு **நாளா**, ஒரு **வாரமா**.

sentences.en: No water at all is coming out of the tap.
The heater hasn't worked for two days.
When I press this switch, the fan doesn't come on.
The tap's been leaking since yesterday.
The power hasn't been right for a week.
The power still hasn't come back.
Even with the heater on, the water doesn't get hot.
Nobody at all has come for three days.
The fan's broken down.
The switch is faulty, be careful.

lessons.title: Getting the owner to fix it

tip.title: Getting it done: -அச் சொல்லு · -அ வை · -இக் குடு
tip.body:
- 'Get X to come' = tell X to come: பிளம்பரை **வரச் சொல்லுங்க**.
- 'Make it happen': infinitive + **வை**: சரி பண்ண **வைக்கிறேன்** 'I'll get it fixed'.
- 'Do it for me': -இ form + **குடு**: மாத்திக் **குடுங்க**.
- Verb pairs: மாறு 'change (by itself)' → **மாத்து** 'change, replace something'.

sentences.en: The owner told the plumber to come.
Get the electrician to come this evening.
Please replace this tap for me.

sentences.native: வீட்டுக்காரருக்கு ஃபோன் பண்ணி சரி பண்ண வைக்கிறேன்.
sentences.roman: vīṭṭukkārarukku fōn paṇṇi sari paṇṇa vaikkirēn.
sentences.en: I'll call the owner and get it fixed.
The plumber came and replaced the tap.
We need to get the heater replaced with a new one.
He only turns up on time to collect the rent!
Apparently the electrician won't come till tomorrow.
He's not even picking up the phone.

tip.title: போடு and வை: switching on, locking, putting
tip.body:
- **போடு** 'put (in/on)' also means **switch on**: மோட்டார் போடு, ஃபேன் போடு — and **lock up**: பூட்டு போடு.
- **வை** 'put, keep, leave': குப்பையை வெளியே வைங்க 'put the rubbish out'.
- 'Switch off' is **ஆஃப் பண்ணு**.

sentences.en: There's no water in the tank, switch on the pump.
Ask the watchman to switch the pump on.

sentences.native: அரை மணி நேரம் கழிச்சு மோட்டாரை ஆஃப் பண்ணுங்க.
sentences.roman: arai maṇi nēram kaḻicchu mōṭṭārai āf paṇṇunga.
sentences.en: Switch the pump off after half an hour.

sentences.native: குப்பையை காலையில ஏழு மணிக்குள்ள வெளியே வைங்க.
sentences.roman: kuppaiyai kālaiyila ēḻu maṇikkuḷḷa veḷiyē vainga.
sentences.en: Put the rubbish out by seven in the morning.
Lock the door when you go out.
Leave your bike in the parking, not on the street.

sentences.native: வாட்ச்மேன் ராத்திரி பதினொரு மணிக்கு பூட்டு போட்டுடுவாரு.
sentences.roman: vāṭchmēn rāttiri padinoru maṇikku pūṭṭu pōṭṭuḍuvāru.
sentences.en: The watchman locks up at eleven at night.
The lift hasn't been working for two days.
How much is the maintenance this month?
If there's a water problem, tell the watchman.

tip.title: Asking the neighbours nicely
tip.body:
- Call neighbours **அக்கா, அண்ணா** (your age) or **ஆன்ட்டி, அங்கிள்** (older), and use நீங்க.
- Turn a complaint into a question: present tense + **-ஆ?** — குறைக்கி**றீங்களா?** 'would you reduce…?', வைக்கி**றீங்களா?** 'would you put…?'.
- Small talk first, complaint second.

sentences.native: அக்கா, ராத்திரி கொஞ்சம் டிவி சத்தத்தைக் குறைக்கிறீங்களா?
sentences.roman: akkā, rāttiri konjam ṭīvi sattattaik kuraikkirīngaḷā?
sentences.en: Akka, could you turn the TV down a bit at night?
Anna, would you leave your bike in the parking?
Would you put the rubbish in the bin, please?

sentences.native: சாயங்காலம் கொஞ்சம் மோட்டார் போடுறீங்களா? நான் வர லேட் ஆகும்.
sentences.roman: sāyangālam konjam mōṭṭār pōḍurīngaḷā? nān vara lēṭ āgum.
sentences.en: Could you switch on the pump this evening? I'll be back late.

sentences.native: ஒரு நாள் எங்க வீட்டுக்கு சாப்பிட வர்றீங்களா?
sentences.roman: oru nāḷ enga vīṭṭukku sāppiḍa varrīngaḷā?
sentences.en: Will you come over for a meal one day?
Akka, would you give me your phone number?
The people next door are really nice.
There are loads of mosquitoes in this area.
I don't know anyone in the neighbourhood yet.

sentences.native: மாடி ஜன்னலை சாயங்காலம் சாத்துறீங்களா? கொசு உள்ள வருது.
sentences.roman: māḍi jannalai sāyangālam sātturīngaḷā? kosu uḷḷa varudu.
sentences.en: Would you shut the upstairs window in the evenings? The mosquitoes are getting in.

sentences.native: அடுத்த வாரம் அண்ணா நகருக்கு ஷிஃப்ட் பண்றோம்.
sentences.roman: aḍutta vāram Aṇṇā Nagarukku shifṭ paṇrōm.
sentences.en: We're moving to Anna Nagar next week.

sentences.native: வீட்டைக் காலி பண்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி சுத்தம் பண்ணணும்.
sentences.roman: vīṭṭaik kāli paṇradukku munnāḍi suttam paṇṇaṇum.
sentences.en: We have to clean the house before we hand it back.

sentences.native: ஆள் வச்சு சாமான் எல்லாம் எடுத்துட்டுப் போகலாம்.
sentences.roman: āḷ vacchu sāmān ellām eḍuttuṭṭup pōgalām.
sentences.en: We can get people in to carry all the stuff.

sentences.native: ஷிஃப்ட் பண்ண ஒரு குட்டி யானை புக் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
sentences.roman: shifṭ paṇṇa oru kuṭṭi yānai buk paṇṇiṭṭēn.
sentences.en: I've booked a 'baby elephant' (mini truck) for the move.

sentences.native: எல்லா சாமானும் போயிடுச்சு, வீடு காலியா இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: ellā sāmānum pōyiḍucchu, vīḍu kāliyā irukku.
sentences.en: All the stuff has gone; the house is empty.
Will the owner give the deposit back?
They'll only keep back the money for painting.
Leave the key with the watchman when you go.
